ANSWER: The **global** behaviour (Record A) applies. The observation cursor in this integration is one filter-independent durable position over the store's commit order, shared by all readers — not a per-consumer position.

WHY THE TWO RECORDS CANNOT BE ADJUDICATED AGAINST EACH OTHER
- `docs/engineering/09-observation-contract-a.md` (global) and `09-observation-contract-b.md` (per-consumer) both claim "Version scope: current pinned line"/"Status: normative" and directly contradict. Neither has a date, a supersession marker, or any inbound reference (grep for "observation cursor", "observation-contract", "Record A/B", "per-consumer", "shared by all" hits only these two files).
- Neither is in the curated archive index `docs/engineering/README.md`, which enumerates the archive (00–36) and assigns `09` to `09-adaptive-allocation-spec.md`. So the archive's own precedence rule ("两处冲突时以工程档案中的规格为准") cannot break the tie: both are equally unlisted, equally "normative" orphans.
- The decision therefore must come from the integration itself.

EVIDENCE FROM THE INTEGRATION (workspace = Palimpsest v0.1.2 pinned to Ordarium v1.3.1; `package.json`, installed `@ordarium/core@1.3.1`)
- The only "observation cursor" on the consumed Ordarium surface is the managed-state change feed added by Ordarium spec ORD-BOOT-0 (`StateChangeFeed` / `StateStore.changes()`); `node_modules/@ordarium/core/dist/src/types.d.ts`:
  - `StateChangeFilter` — "Optional narrowing for the revisioned state change feed (ORD-BOOT-0)… Restrict observation to one namespace."
  - `StateChangePage.cursor` — "Opaque, **filter-independent** durable position of the last delivered change", "a consumer reaches the end of the feed and still holds a durable resume position".
- The pinned durable ledger implements exactly that (`node_modules/@ordarium/ledger-sqlite/dist/src/index.js`, `changes()`): "Semantic validation against the **global high-water mark** (ORD-BOOT-0.1): the cursor is a **global, filter-independent position**, so this compares against the whole ledger, not the requested namespace's last sequence." The high-water mark is `SELECT MAX(change_seq) FROM ordarium_state_changes`, and `migrations.js` defines `change_seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` — one monotonic sequence across all namespaces. `migrateFromV3` (ORD-BOOT-0 §7) states v3 "recorded no **global commit order**… From v4 on, every new commit carries the real durable database order."
- The volatile reference ledger (`@ordarium/core` MemoryLedger `changes()`) agrees: positions are contiguous 1..n in one global `#stateChanges` list; the namespace filter only chooses which entries are delivered, it never changes the position space.
- Fail-closed semantics also presuppose one global position: `InvalidCursorError` = "A caller-supplied change-feed cursor could not be decoded as a durable position (ORD-BOOT-0)… fails closed instead of silently restarting from the beginning of the feed."

CONCLUSION
Record A ("global — one position shared by all readers of the store") describes the integration; Record B ("per-consumer — each consumer holds its own independent position") is contradicted: the cursor encodes no consumer identity, is validated against the whole-ledger high-water mark, and is filter-independent, so every reader indexes the same position space. (Not to be confused with Palimpsest's own per-projection `projection_cursors`, or its EventCursor/ViewCursor in spec 35 — those are different concepts, not the "observation cursor".) No peer contact was needed: the pinned dependency artifact resolves the conflict locally.

ANSWER: The GLOBAL behaviour governs the observation cursor at this integration. "Per-consumer" is true only for cursor *ownership* (host-side checkpointing), not for the position space. Resolved by the Ordarium kernel owner (peer ordarium.main, decision evt_d6ff1beb-39ae-4dc8-b71d-f8d85e02ceab, thread thr_447f288d-5213-41ce-9475-485b484a7af5).

WHY THE LOCAL RECORDS COULDN'T DECIDE IT
docs/engineering/09-observation-contract-a.md (global) and -b.md (per-consumer) are both self-labelled "normative, current scope", with no date/supersession, and neither is listed in docs/engineering/README.md (which assigns 09 to 09-adaptive-allocation-spec.md). The archive alone cannot adjudicate them; the observation-cursor contract is Ordarium-owned, so the authority basis had to come from ordarium.main.

AUTHORITATIVE BASIS (owner + revision)
- Owner spec: ORD-BOOT-0 §5 — docs/research/ORD-BOOT-0-state-change-feed-spec.md, frozen 2026-09-11.
- Current revision: ORD-BOOT-0.1 §5 — docs/research/ORD-BOOT-0.1-state-change-feed-hardening-spec.md, frozen 2026-09-11 (patch 1.3.1); supersedes ORD-BOOT-0 §5 future-cursor behaviour and §7 limit domain ONLY.
- Normative docs of record: docs/13-ordarium-action-contract.md §11 (ORDARIUM-ACTION-2), docs/14 §1, docs/17 §16.11/16.12 (ORDARIUM-GOALS-3); docs/dev/04-errors.md (INVALID_CURSOR = position outside the ledger's global high-water).
- Cross-checked against the pinned artifacts this workspace consumes: @ordarium/core 1.3.1 StateChangePage.cursor = "opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change"; @ordarium/ledger-sqlite 1.3.1 changes() = WHERE c.change_seq > ? [+optional namespace] ORDER BY c.change_seq ASC, validated against MAX(change_seq) over the whole ordarium_state_changes table.

THE EXACT SPLIT (peer decision)
1) POSITION SPACE = global. One durable ledger commit-observation order (ordarium_state_changes.change_seq, AUTOINCREMENT, assigned in the same transaction as the state CAS). A cursor means "skip everything with position <= C, ledger-wide"; it is filter-independent and reusable across namespaces/filters. This is Record A.
2) CURSOR OWNERSHIP = host/consumer-side, over the same global space. Ordarium keeps no consumer offsets, subscription registry, acks or delivery leases (ORD-BOOT-0 §2 non-goals; §6 delivery = AtLeastOnceObservation + DurableCursor + IdempotentConsumerPossible); each consumer persists its own copy of the last returned global position. So "each consumer holds its own independent position" is true as ownership, false as a per-consumer/per-namespace position space or local sequence — Record B does not govern the position space.

SCOPE DISTINCTION
Only StateChangeFeed.changes() (i.e. StateStore.changes()) is the observation cursor at this seam. The nextCursor? of operation list/history and of stateHistory/listStates/listStatesReferencing are per-scan (stateHistory per-subject) pagination cursors — not durable observation positions. Record B must not be applied to the change feed if derived from those surfaces.

BOUNDARY HYGIENE
Opened boundary thread thr_447f288d-5213-41ce-9475-485b484a7af5 and proposed BoundaryContract palimpsest-ordarium.observation-cursor (revision 1, termsDigest 8eb63b8e0b19e3c158f713753003c541fc7727f1766e4df2b079315d3ac5557f) to establish the authority basis; peer batch bat_a1dbd2a6-27a1-4a7c-9fe7-48481e1c16ed received and acked.
